thread.title: NBCUniversal to launch ad-supported streaming service in 2019

author: Mike Murphy
title: NBCUniversal to launch ad-supported streaming service in 2019
text:
An earlier headline mistakenly said the service would launch in 2019. It its expected to launch in 2020.
NBC Ted Danson and Kristen Bell star in NBC’s “The Good Place.” Add one more major player to the streaming wars.
Comcast Corp.’s CMCSA, +0.39% NBCUniversal announced Monday it will launch a free, ad-supported streaming service in the first quarter of 2020. According to a report by CNBC , the service will be free to cable subscribers, and available for around $12 a month for those without a cable provider. It will reportedly air three to five minutes of commercials per hour, and will also offer an ad-free tier for an additional fee. Essentially, it will be more along the lines of Hulu or CBS All Access than Netflix or Amazon’s AMZN, -1.42% Prime Video.
CNBC reported the service will include 1,500 hours of NBCU content, such as “Saturday Night Live” and “Parks & Recreation,” and Universal Pictures movies. The service will also include live sports, including the 2020 Summer Olympics, and licensed content from other studios, such as Sony SNE, -1.14% , Discovery DISCA, -0.44% and Warner Bros., CNBC said.
The report added that NBCU is not expected to pull its content from other streaming services. For example, reruns of “The Office,” which was produced by NBCUniversal Television, are a huge hit for Netflix Inc. NFLX, -1.38% , which owns its exclusive streaming rights through 2021. NBCU could, in theory, grant Netflix non-exclusive streaming rights after that, collecting licensing fees while also airing it on its own service — much like the deal WarnerMedia made in December with Netflix over “Friends.”
NBCU’s service is expected to launch shortly after the debuts of rival streaming services from AT&T’s T, -0.81% WarnerMedia and Disney DIS, -0.20% , scheduled for late 2019. Apple Inc. AAPL, -1.50% is also expected to launch its streaming service this year or next.
The news raises more questions about the future of Hulu, which is 30% owned by NBCUniversal. There has been speculation that NBCU may seek to sell its stake once Disney completes its acquisition of Fox FOX, -0.12% assets, which will give it 60% control of Hulu.
The move is also a reversal in strategy for NBCU parent Comcast. As recently as October, Comcast CEO Brian Roberts said his company was in no hurry to start a streaming service. “Streaming, we think, is very challenging economically, and we don’t want to rush into anything,” he said, according to AdWeek.
As part of Monday’s announcement, NBCUniversal CEO Steve Burke laid out a number of management changes: cable chief Bonnie Hammer will take over the streaming service, while NBC Sports chief Mark Lazarus and Universal Chairman Jeff Shell will take on expanded roles. Donna Langley will take over as chairman of Universal Filmed Entertainment.
Comcast shares are up 5% year to date, but down nearly 16% over the past 12 months, compared to the S&P 500’s SPX, -0.53% 3% rise in 2019 and 7% decline over the past year.
